info.name: fxapis — MetaTrader 5 REST API
info.description:
The fxapis MetaTrader 5 REST API: connect MT5 accounts, place market and pending orders,
manage positions, read orders and deals, and place one order across many accounts at once.

Full documentation: https://docs.fxapis.com

**Set `apiKey`** (collection variables) to your key. Test keys (`fx_test_…`) still reach real
brokers — connect a broker *demo* MT5 account while you try things out.

**Set `adminKey`** to an admin key (`fx_admin_…`) to use the *API keys* folder. Only the workspace
owner can make one, in the console; it manages keys and can do nothing else.

Every POST and PATCH gets an `Idempotency-Key` automatically (see the collection pre-request
script): re-sending the same key returns the first answer, a new key means a new order.

---

fxapis is the MetaTrader 5 API. Connect an MT5 account once, then trade it, read its positions
and its history over plain HTTP. Choose whether each account stays connected or comes online
only when you need it.

### Conventions

- Every successful response is `{ "data": … }`; every failure is `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`.
  Match on `code`, which is stable. `message` is written for a human and may change.
- Every response carries `requestId`. Quote it in a support request and the entire call can be found.
- Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. Money and prices are never floats in a request body.

### Bringing an account online is not instant

A broker login takes as long as the broker takes — usually seconds, occasionally much longer.
`POST /accounts/{id}/warm` brings an account online and returns **202** with a `pollUrl` rather than
holding the request open, so your client's timeout never becomes a question about someone else's
network. Poll `GET /accounts/{id}/status` until `state` is `ready`.

### Credentials

The MT5 password you send is encrypted before it is stored, with a data key that is bound to that
one account, and is never returned by any endpoint, written to the account record or included in
a log line. We cannot show it back to you — if it is lost, it is reset at the broker.

item.name: Accounts
item.description: Connecting MT5 accounts and reading their state.

request.description:
Every account in this workspace, newest first.

`GET /v1/accounts`

Stores the account and encrypts its password. It does **not** log in: the account lands in `created`, and connects when you bring it online or when the first order arrives on a `warm_on_demand` account.

**Reconnecting.** If this login and server were connected before and then disconnected, the same account comes back — its id and history kept — with the new password, and the answer is `200` instead of `201`. If they are still connected, the answer is `409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS` with the account's id; to change its password, use `POST /v1/accounts/{id}/password`.

`POST /v1/accounts`

One connected account: its login, server, label, mode, current state and when it last changed. The password is never included. Another workspace's account is 404. Balance, equity and margin are the last read from the terminal (`figuresObservedAt`); `GET /v1/accounts/{id}/figures?fresh=true` asks it now.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}`

item.name: Delete an account and its history

query.description: `true` deletes even with open positions, which stay open at the broker.

request.description:
Removes the account for good: its terminal is stopped, its password erased, and the record deleted with its orders, deals and positions. **This cannot be undone.** To stop trading on an account but keep its history readable, disconnect it instead.

Refused with `409` while an order is in flight (`ACCOUNT_EXECUTING`), while a multi-account order that includes it has not finished (`ACCOUNT_IN_WAVE`), and when our last look found open positions (`ACCOUNT_HAS_POSITIONS`): those stay open at the broker with their stops, but could no longer be shown or closed here. Close them first, or send `force=true` to delete anyway.

Alert hooks stop sending to the account; a hook left with no accounts is switched off. This month's usage is unaffected. The same login and server can be connected again afterwards, as a new account.

`DELETE /v1/accounts/{id}`

The endpoint to poll after bringing an account online. Cheap enough to call every second or two; `state` reaches `ready` when the account is logged in and ready to trade.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/status`

query.description: `true` asks the account's terminal now (the account must be online), charged to the account's live budget when the terminal is asked. Without it, the last read.

request.description:
The account's money as its MetaTrader terminal reports it: balance, equity, margin, free margin, margin level, credit and open profit, as decimal strings in the account's currency.

Without `fresh`, the last read: taken every 15 seconds while the account is online, with `observedAt` saying when. With `fresh=true`, the terminal is asked now — the account must be `ready` (409 `ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` otherwise, including while it is `executing` an order or `degraded`); a terminal still on an older worker answers 501 `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` instead, rare in practice. Callers within the same second share one read, and only a read that reaches the terminal is charged to the account's live budget (300 a minute + 50 across every caller; 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after` past it).

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/figures`

Gives a connected account a new trading password — after the member changed it at the broker, or when the account is in `invalid_credentials` because the one it had was wrong. Send `server` as well to correct the server name.

The account is taken offline first (refused with `409` while an order is in flight), the new password is encrypted and stored, and only then is the old one erased — a failure leaves the old credential in place. The account lands in `created` and comes online on the next order or when you bring it online; bring it online straight away to check the new password while the member is still there. The password is never returned or logged.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/password`

item.name: Move an account to another server

request.description:
For a login refused because it was added under the wrong server name: keeps the stored password and tries it on `server` instead, so the password is not sent again. The broker's likely servers are in the account's `problem.otherServers`. With `connect: true` (the default) the account is brought online straight away, so the answer comes back in seconds — watch `state`, or the account's events.

`409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS` when that login is already connected on that server here; `409 NO_PASSWORD` when no password is stored (send one to `/password` instead).

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/server`

The account's history in words, newest first: added, logging in, refused by the broker, online, moved to another server, taken offline. The same record the console shows as the account's activity.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/events`

MT5 servers matching what someone typed — a broker's name (`vantage`), the start of a server name (`JustMarkets-De`), with or without dashes and spaces. Built for a typeahead in your connect form: call it as the person types (debounced, from 2 characters) and let them pick.

Servers accounts on fxapis have logged in to come first (`proven: true`), then names starting with what was typed, then the kind asked for (`demo`/`live`), then the broker's main server. With fewer than five matches for 3+ characters, the broker search is asked once and its servers added, so a broker nobody here has used yet is found too — that call can take a second or two.

**A server that is not listed can still be connected**: always let people use exactly what they typed. Without `q`, the servers used most here.

`GET /v1/brokers/servers`

item.name: Lifecycle
item.description: Bringing an account online, taking it offline, and changing how it stays connected.

request.description:
Starts connecting the account and returns **202** immediately — the broker login is still in progress. Poll `pollUrl` until `state` is `ready`.

Calling this for an account that is already online is harmless and returns `alreadyRunning: true`, so a client that is unsure can simply call it.

Returns 409 when the account needs a human first (a wrong password, 2FA, a certificate, trading disabled at the broker). Retrying will not fix those, and repeated failed logins are how a broker locks an account.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/warm`

item.name: Bring several accounts online at once

request.description:
Brings every account listed online and returns **202** with a result for each — the broker logins are still in progress. Built for a signal: call it when the signal goes out, and by the time people act on it their accounts are online, so the order goes straight through instead of waiting for a login.

An account already online is reported as `already_running`; one that needs a human first (`needs_operator`) is not retried. `warm_on_demand` accounts go offline again by themselves after the idle window with no orders.

`POST /v1/accounts/prepare`

Takes the account offline and keeps it, with its stored password, in `standby` — ready to be brought online again. Open positions are untouched: a stop loss or take profit is held by the broker and keeps working while the account is offline.

Returns 409 while an order is in flight. Going offline then would turn a known outcome into an unknown one, and a retry on top of that is a duplicate trade.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/cool`

For an account that is online but misbehaving — `degraded`, stale quotes, a stuck sync. Returns **202**; poll `pollUrl` until `state` is `ready`. Refused with 409 while an order is in flight, for the same reason as taking it offline.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/restart`

Takes the account offline and **deletes the stored password**. The account record stays, with its history, in `offline`. Reconnecting means sending the password again.

This is the endpoint to call when a customer leaves. A disconnected account that still holds a usable password is a credential nobody is watching.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/disconnect`

item.name: Change how eagerly the account stays connected

request.description:
`always_on`: stays connected. `warm_on_demand`: connects on demand (the first order, or a prepare) and goes offline by itself when idle. `cold`: connects only when you ask.

Takes effect the next time the account is brought online, so the call stays fast and predictable. Switch to `always_on` and then bring the account online to apply it now.

A copy-trading strategy's account must stay `always_on`: moving it to another mode is refused with 409 `ACCOUNT_IS_MASTER` until the strategy is archived.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/mode`

item.name: Instruments
item.description: Markets named once — `XAUUSD`, `US30`, `BTCUSD` — and how each maps onto an account's broker symbols. An order can name an `instrument` instead of a `symbol`, and trades that account's own symbol for it.

item.name: List the instruments a signal can name

query.description: Only this category.

request.description:
The markets fxapis names once, whatever each broker calls them: currency pairs, metals, indices, energies and crypto. A signal that names one of these as `instrument` is traded on every account under that account's own broker symbol. Needs no account and no broker.

`GET /v1/instruments`

item.name: List the symbols an account's broker offers

query.description: Only symbols whose name or description contains this.
Only symbols this account can, or cannot, open positions in.
The `nextCursor` from the previous page.

request.description:
Every symbol the account's broker offers it, with its contract specification, as read from the broker when the account was last online — so it answers while the account is offline. Refreshed each time the account comes online and the list is a day old. `syncedAt` says when.

Returns 409 `SYMBOLS_NOT_SYNCED` for an account that has never been online.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/symbols`

item.name: See how each instrument maps onto an account's broker

request.description:
For every instrument, the symbol an order naming it will trade on this account — or why it cannot: the broker has several plausible symbols (`ambiguous`, with `candidates`), or does not offer it (`missing`). Useful when a member connects, to tell them which signals their account can follow.

A symbol is mapped automatically only when its name matches and, where the market has one standard contract, its contract size agrees: gold quoted per gram is never taken for gold per ounce.

Returns 409 `SYMBOLS_NOT_SYNCED` for an account that has never been online.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/instruments`

item.name: Market hours for a symbol or instrument, from the account's broker

query.description: A broker symbol, exactly as the broker spells it.
Or an instrument, e.g. `XAUUSD`: this account's symbol for it is used.

request.description:
When the account's broker lets orders be placed in a symbol — or in this account's symbol for an instrument — as the broker configured it (MetaTrader's `SymbolInfoSessionTrade`), with whether it is open now and when that next changes.

`trade` and `quote` are given in the broker's server time and in UTC; `utcOffsetSeconds` is the broker's clock as measured when the sessions were read. Read when the account comes online and refreshed daily, so it answers while the account is offline.

Holidays a broker does not load into its schedule are not here: on such a day an order is still refused with `ORDER_REJECTED` (`Market closed`).

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/sessions`

item.name: Read an account's symbols from its broker now

request.description:
Reads the broker's symbol list again and remaps the instruments, for when the broker has added symbols. Needs the account online (`ready`); returns 409 `ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` otherwise. It happens on its own once a day while the account is online, so most integrations never call this.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/symbols/sync`

item.name: Trading
item.description: Placing orders and reading positions. The endpoints that move money.

header.description: Postman fills in a fresh UUID on every send. Re-sending the same key (with the same body) returns the first answer instead of placing a second order; a new key means a new order. To retry safely, replace `{{$guid}}` with a fixed value.

request.description:
Sends a market order and waits for the broker's answer.

**Send an `Idempotency-Key` header.** Without one, a request that times out leaves you unable to retry safely: you cannot tell whether the order was placed, and guessing wrong opens a second position. With one, retrying is free — the same key returns the same answer and never places a second order.

Three failures are worth telling apart, and the response distinguishes them:

- **`SEND_FAILED` (503)** — nothing reached the broker. Resend only when `retryable` is `true`; it is `false` when the order was taken from this request before it could go (cancelled, say), so look at the order first.
- **`ORDER_REJECTED` (422)** — the broker refused it, with a reason and its own return code. `retryable` says whether the reason was transient (a requote, a moved price) or permanent (insufficient margin, a closed market).
- **`ORDER_UNRESOLVED` (503)** — we do not know. The order may be live at the broker. It is in `unknown` while we confirm the result with the broker. **Do not resend it**; poll the order instead.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/orders/market`

header.description: Postman fills in a fresh UUID on every send. Re-sending the same key (with the same body) returns the first answer instead of placing a second order; a new key means a new order. To retry safely, replace `{{$guid}}` with a fixed value.

request.description:
Closes a position in whole, or partly if you send a `volume`.

**Send an `Idempotency-Key`.** It matters more here than on an opening order: a retried close does not close twice, it opens an opposing position, and the account ends up with exposure nobody chose.

The three failure modes are the same as for an opening order, and `ORDER_UNRESOLVED` means the same thing — **do not resend**, poll the order. An unresolved close is the case where you might believe you are flat and not be.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/positions/{positionId}/close`

item.name: Move a position's stop loss or take profit

request.description:
**Send `null` to remove a level.** Omitting the field leaves it unchanged — an omitted field silently clearing a stop is how protection disappears without anybody choosing it.

Recorded in the order history with intent `modify`, because widening a stop changes what the account risks and belongs beside the trade it protects.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/positions/{positionId}/modify`

item.name: Place a limit, stop or stop-limit order

header.description: Postman fills in a fresh UUID on every send. Re-sending the same key (with the same body) returns the first answer instead of placing a second order; a new key means a new order. To retry safely, replace `{{$guid}}` with a fixed value.

request.description:
A success here means **placed and waiting**, not filled — the broker answers `10008 PLACED` and the order is `working` until it triggers.

A limit waits for a better price (buy below the market, sell above); a stop waits for a worse one and is how a breakout is traded (buy above, sell below). When fxapis has a recent price for the symbol on this account, the wrong side is refused before anything is sent, with a message naming the order you probably meant; otherwise the broker answers with its own `INVALID_PRICE`.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/orders/pending`

item.name: Move a pending order's price or levels

request.description:
Keeps the order's ticket. Cancelling and re-placing loses its place in the broker's queue and leaves a window where the order does not exist at all — on a fast market that window is where the move happens.

An omitted field is left alone. Send `stopLoss: null` to clear a stop; omitting it keeps whatever is there.

Only an order in `working` can be moved. A `filled` order is a position — move its stop with `/positions/{id}/modify` instead.

`POST /v1/orders/{id}/modify`

Removes a pending order that has not triggered. If it already has, the broker refuses with `10035` — at that point there is a position, not an order, and what you want is a close.

`POST /v1/orders/{id}/cancel`

item.name: Margin required, or profit at a price

request.description:
Opens nothing and is safe to call freely. This is how you find out an order will be refused for margin *before* sending it, rather than collecting a `10019` from the broker.

The account must be online: an offline account is refused with 409 `NO_RUNTIME`. A null `value` means the broker would not answer, which is not the same as zero.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/calculate`

item.name: Confirm pending results with the broker now

request.description:
Confirms the result of every opening order on this account still in `unknown`, and brings its deals and positions up to date with the broker. A close, stop change or cancel in `unknown` is not settled from deal history — its `stateDetail` says to check the position or order at the broker.

This happens automatically; call it when you do not want to wait. It is safe to call at any time and safe to call twice — nothing is recorded or settled twice.

`ambiguous` counts orders whose result the broker's records do not settle unambiguously. Those are left in `unknown` on purpose: a wrong guess produces a history that looks settled and is wrong, which is worse than the gap. They need a human.

`skipped` is `no-runtime` when the account is offline: bring it online and call again.

`POST /v1/accounts/{id}/reconcile`

query.description: `true` also returns positions we have seen closed, with `closedAt` set.

request.description:
What we last saw, with `observedAt` saying when. The broker is authoritative and this is a snapshot, not a ledger — `observedAt` is here so you can tell a current view from a stale one rather than having to assume.

Open positions only, unless `includeClosed=true`.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/positions`

item.name: Market data
item.description: Prices from each account's own broker, read live from its terminal. Each broker quotes differently, and these are the prices that account trades at.

item.name: Live prices from the account's broker

query.description: Broker symbols, comma-separated, exactly as this broker names them: `EURUSD.a,XAUUSD.a`.
Instruments (`GET /v1/instruments`), comma-separated; each is quoted as this account's own symbol for it.

request.description:
Bid, ask and spread for up to 20 symbols or instruments, read from the account's own MetaTrader terminal — the prices this account trades at. The account must be online (409 `ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` otherwise).

Every quote carries `time`, `brokerTime` and `ageMs`; judge freshness from them. `stale` is true only while the market is open and the last tick is over 60 seconds old; a closed market answers its last price with `marketOpen: false`. A symbol the broker does not have answers `status: unknown_symbol` in its place. Poll this; there is no stream. Calls that reach the terminal are charged to the account's live budget (300 a minute + 50, across every caller; cached answers are free), and past it this answers 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `retry-after`. An account whose terminal is still on an older worker — rare — answers 501 `CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` instead.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/quotes`

item.name: History
item.description: The durable record: every order, every deal the broker recorded, and what it returned. Includes deals no order of yours caused.

query.description: Narrow to one account.
`unknown` is the set whose result we are still confirming with the broker.
The `nextCursor` from the previous page.

request.description:
Every order this workspace has placed, newest first, across all accounts unless `accountId` narrows it. Filter by `state` to find what needs attention — `state=unknown` is the set whose result we are still confirming with the broker.

Paginated by cursor rather than offset: an offset shifts as new orders arrive, so page two would silently skip rows.

`GET /v1/orders`

The authoritative record of one order: what was asked for, what the broker returned, and its own return code unmodified. Poll this after an `ORDER_UNRESOLVED` response — an opening order moves out of `unknown` as soon as we have confirmed the result with the broker; a close, stop change or cancel stays `unknown`, with a `stateDetail` saying what to check at the broker.

`GET /v1/orders/{id}`

One order can produce several deals — a partial fill leaves more than one. These are the broker's own records of money changing hands, which is what a statement is reconciled against.

`GET /v1/orders/{id}/deals`

query.description: Only deals on this symbol, as the broker names it.
Deals at or after this time (the broker's timestamp).
Deals at or before this time.
The `nextCursor` from the previous page.

request.description:
Everything the broker recorded against this account, **including deals no order of yours caused** — a stop loss firing, a swap charge, a deposit, or somebody trading the same login from the MetaTrader desktop.

That inclusion is the point. A history containing only your own orders would show an account whose balance moves for no visible reason. Ordered by the broker's timestamp, not ours.

`GET /v1/accounts/{id}/deals`

item.name: Waves
item.description: Multi-account orders: one trade placed on many accounts at once, with a result for each account. For signals that should reach every follower at the same moment.

request.description:
Multi-account orders in this workspace, newest first, with each one's state, symbol, side, number of accounts and summary of results.

`GET /v1/execution-waves`

item.name: Place one trade on many accounts

header.description: Postman fills in a fresh UUID on every send. Re-sending the same key (with the same body) returns the first answer instead of placing a second order; a new key means a new order. To retry safely, replace `{{$guid}}` with a fixed value.

request.description:
A multi-account order: one trade placed on many accounts at once. Every account is brought online first, then the orders are sent together — at `executeAt`, or as soon as every account is online.

**A multi-account order is not all-or-nothing once sent, and cannot be.** There is no transaction across a hundred brokers: accounts fill at different prices, some are rejected for margin, some go unanswered. So it never reports a single success or failure — it reports a result for each account, and `summary` counts what landed. An account whose result is `unresolved` must not be resent; poll its order.

`dispatchSpreadMs` is the gap between the first account's order being sent and the last. It is the number worth watching: as it grows, your accounts are getting different prices.

**`barrierPolicy`** decides what happens when some accounts are not online in time:

- `release-ready` — trade on the accounts that are online, skip the rest. A partial entry beats a late one.
- `all-or-nothing` — trade on none unless all are online. Note this is about *sending*: a broker can still reject an account's order after it was sent.
- `wait` — keep waiting past `executeAt` until every account is online, up to `expiresAt`.

`POST /v1/execution-waves`

Poll this after creating a multi-account order. `state` moves `planned → preparing → armed → releasing → settled`: accepted, bringing accounts online, waiting for `executeAt`, sending, and every account has a result. `cancelled` and `abandoned` mean nothing was sent.

Each account in `legs` carries its own state and its own order id — an account's order is an ordinary order, confirmed with the broker and audited like any other.

`GET /v1/execution-waves/{id}`

item.name: Cancel a multi-account order before it is sent

request.description:
Only while nothing has been sent. Once orders are going out there is no cancelling them — `cancelled` would claim nothing was sent, and that is exactly the promise we can no longer make.

`POST /v1/execution-waves/{id}/cancel`

item.name: Copy trading
item.description: Managed copy trading: mark an always-on account as a strategy, subscribe other accounts in this workspace, and fxapis repeats the master's opens, closes, partial closes and stop moves on every follower, sized for each, with no code on your side. Every decision is an execution with its reason. Hedging accounts only.

request.description:
`paused` true while copy trading is paused on this server (before scheduled maintenance): strategies and subscriptions can be read, paused and deleted, but nothing that starts copying is taken (503 `COPY_TRADING_PAUSED`), nothing is copied, and no follower is billed. `message` says so in a sentence, or is null.

`GET /v1/copy/status`

query.description: Default: `100`.
The previous page's `nextCursor`.

request.description:
This workspace's copy-trading strategies, newest first, archived ones included. Paginated by cursor.

`GET /v1/copy/strategies`

Marks an account as a strategy: its trades are copied to every account that subscribes to it. The account must be `always_on` — a master traded by hand never sends fxapis an order, so an idle terminal would be stopped — and a hedging account, and must not follow a strategy itself. One live strategy per account. A member confirms it is them (step-up). While copy trading is paused on this server (`GET /v1/copy/status`), this answers 503 `COPY_TRADING_PAUSED`.

`POST /v1/copy/strategies`
`GET /v1/copy/strategies/{id}`

item.name: Rename, pause or resume a strategy

request.description:
A paused strategy's master is not watched, and nothing is copied — closes included — until it is resumed; the drift check then puts followers right. Resuming asks a member to confirm it is them (step-up), needs a plan with copy trading, and is refused as a whole (403 `KEY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, naming the account) when the caller may not open on one of the active followers — a connected app's consent list, a key's `accountIds`, or a key with limits and someone else's subscription. Pause that subscription first. Renaming and pausing always work; resuming is refused while copy trading is paused on this server (503 `COPY_TRADING_PAUSED`, `GET /v1/copy/status`).

`PATCH /v1/copy/strategies/{id}`

Only once no subscription copies it (pause or delete them first). Its executions and links stay in the log, and its paused or stopped subscriptions stay, unable to resume; the account can become a strategy again.

`DELETE /v1/copy/strategies/{id}`

query.description: Default: `100`.
The previous page's `nextCursor`.

request.description:
Followers, newest first, with their status, settings, equity, today's profit where the figures allow, and their last execution. Paginated by cursor.

`GET /v1/copy/subscriptions`

item.name: Subscribe an account to a strategy

request.description:
The follower copies the strategy's master from now on, with its own settings; every setting has a default. Same workspace, hedging accounts only, and an account cannot be a master and a follower at once. Counts against the plan's followers when it starts `active`. A member confirms it is them (step-up). While copy trading is paused on this server (`GET /v1/copy/status`), this answers 503 `COPY_TRADING_PAUSED`.

`POST /v1/copy/subscriptions`
`GET /v1/copy/subscriptions/{id}`

item.name: Change a subscription's settings or status

request.description:
`settings` is merged into what is there: objects key by key, lists and `symbols.map` replaced. `status` is `active`, `paused` or `close_only`; a stopped subscription is brought back with POST …/reset. Changing sizing, limits, reverse or risk limits, or resuming, asks a member to confirm it is them (step-up); pausing and close_only never do. Moving into `active` or `close_only` counts against the plan's followers. Moving into `active` is refused while copy trading is paused on this server (503 `COPY_TRADING_PAUSED`, `GET /v1/copy/status`); settings, pausing and close_only still work.

`PATCH /v1/copy/subscriptions/{id}`

`closePositions` is required.

- `true`: the subscription stops at once (`stopped`, `stopReason` `deleted`, `deleting` true) and every position it holds on the follower is closed, by ticket — including one whose copied open is still in flight, once it fills. The closes are recorded before any is sent, so they go even if this request is cut off, and a follower that is offline gets them when it is back. The subscription is removed once they are all closed: 200 with `deleted` true when that happens within this request, otherwise 202 with what is still `pending`. A close the broker refuses (`failed`) keeps the subscription until it is closed: delete again to retry, or with `false` to keep the rest.
- `false`: the subscription is removed now, and its links with it: the positions stay open on the follower as the account's own, no longer copied, closed or corrected by copy trading (`released` counts them).

Either way the executions log is kept, with `subscriptionId` null.

`DELETE /v1/copy/subscriptions/{id}`

Back to `active` (or to `paused`, if it was paused when it stopped), with every risk period measured afresh from the next figures read. Back to `active` counts against the plan's followers. Needs a plan with copy trading, and asks a member to confirm it is them (step-up). A stop-out's closes still pending keep going. While copy trading is paused on this server (`GET /v1/copy/status`), this answers 503 `COPY_TRADING_PAUSED`.

`POST /v1/copy/subscriptions/{id}/reset`

query.description: Default: `"open"`.

request.description:
Which follower position copies which master position. Closes, partial closes and the drift check go through these, never by symbol. Open links only, or with `state=all` those closed in the last 30 days too.

`GET /v1/copy/subscriptions/{id}/links`

query.description: Only executions created at or after this moment.
Default: `50`.
The previous page's `nextCursor`.

request.description:
The copy-trading log: what each master change (and each drift correction or stop-out close) did on each follower, newest first — executed, skipped, failed or still pending — with the reason, in words, and the follower's order. Paginated by cursor.

`GET /v1/copy/executions`

item.name: Alerts
item.description: TradingView alert hooks: a secret URL that turns TradingView alerts into orders on your accounts, with no EA and no VPS. The URL is returned once, when a hook is created or rotated.

request.description:
Newest first. Deleted hooks are not listed. The URLs are shown only as hints — the secret is not stored.

`GET /v1/alert-hooks`

Returns a secret `url` to paste into a TradingView alert's **Webhook URL**. Every alert sent to it becomes an order on the hook's accounts: one account places an ordinary order, several place a multi-account order.

**The URL is returned once**, here, and is a credential: anyone who has it can trade these accounts. We store only a hash of it. Lost or leaked, rotate it.

`defaults` fill in what an alert leaves out and translate TradingView's symbols to your broker's. See the TradingView guide for the message format.

Several accounts need a plan with multi-account orders; that is checked here, and again on every alert.

`POST /v1/alert-hooks`

One alert hook: its name, accounts, defaults, whether it is enabled and when it was last used. The secret URL is never returned again — rotate the hook for a new one.

`GET /v1/alert-hooks/{id}`

item.name: Change an alert hook's name, accounts or defaults

request.description:
The URL does not change, so nothing needs editing in TradingView. `defaults` fields you send replace those fields; the rest stay as they are. `symbolMap`, when sent, replaces the whole map.

`PATCH /v1/alert-hooks/{id}`

Its URL stops working at once and cannot be brought back. Orders it placed stay in the history, with the alert that caused them in `clientOrderId`.

`DELETE /v1/alert-hooks/{id}`

Issues a new secret URL and retires the old one at once: alerts still pointing at it are refused from now on. Update every TradingView alert that uses it. The new `url` is returned **once**.

`POST /v1/alert-hooks/{id}/rotate`

Alerts are traded again from the next one. Safe to repeat.

`POST /v1/alert-hooks/{id}/enable`

Alerts are refused — answered 409 and recorded as `rejected` — until it is enabled again. The URL stays the same, so nothing changes in TradingView. Safe to repeat.

`POST /v1/alert-hooks/{id}/disable`

item.name: Alerts a hook received, and what became of each

query.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`.

request.description:
Newest first, kept for 30 days. The first place to look when an alert did not trade: every alert that reached a hook is here — refused, ignored and duplicate ones included — with the reason in words.

A hook takes at most 30 alerts a minute; past that, one row records the refusal and the rest of that minute's alerts are not recorded.

`GET /v1/alert-hooks/{id}/deliveries`

item.name: Webhooks
item.description: Event webhooks: a signed POST to your HTTPS endpoint when an order fills or is rejected, a position opens or closes, an account changes state, or a multi-account order finishes. Retried over about 44.6 hours (jittered), with a delivery log and redelivery. The signing secret is returned once, when an endpoint is created or rotated. Needs `webhooks:write`. See the webhooks guide for event types and verifying signatures.

request.description:
Newest first. Deleted endpoints are not listed. Secrets are never returned here.

`GET /v1/webhooks`

Events are POSTed to `url` as JSON — `{ id, type, createdAt, data }` — signed in the `fxapis-signature` header with the returned `secret`. **The secret is returned once**, here. Retried over about 44.6 hours on failure (jittered; the last wait alone can run up to about 28.8 hours); switched off after 20 failures in a row. Up to 10 endpoints per workspace.

`POST /v1/webhooks`

With its health: the last delivery, failures in a row, and why it was switched off if it was.

`GET /v1/webhooks/{id}`

Change its `url`, `events` or `description`. The secret stays the same.

`PATCH /v1/webhooks/{id}`

Nothing more is sent to it, including retries in progress. Cannot be undone.

`DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}`

Events are sent again from the next one, and the failure count starts from zero. Deliveries that were waiting when it was switched off resume on their schedule. Events recorded while it was off are not sent automatically — replay them (`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/replay`, failed-only by default), or read them from `GET /v1/events`. Safe to repeat.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/enable`

Events stop being sent to it until it is enabled again. Deliveries already waiting are kept, not dropped; events recorded meanwhile can be replayed once it is back. Safe to repeat.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/disable`

Issues a new `secret`, returned **once**. For 24 hours every delivery is signed with both the new and the old secret — two `v1=` values in `fxapis-signature` — so you can deploy the new one without missing an event.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate`

Sends a `webhook.test` event to this endpoint only, within a few seconds. Check the delivery log for the result.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test`

item.name: Delivery attempts to a webhook endpoint

query.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`.

request.description:
Every attempt, newest first, kept 30 days: what was sent, what your endpoint answered, and how long it took.

`GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries`

The request as sent — URL, headers (signature included) and exact body — and what your endpoint answered: status, headers and the first 4 KB of the body. Latency is `durationMs`. Kept 30 days on every plan, even once the event itself has aged out of your event history.

`GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}`

Queues the event to this endpoint again, with a fresh retry schedule. Same event id, so your deduplication still works.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{eventId}/redeliver`

Queues this window's events, of the types this endpoint receives, oldest first, with their original ids. By default (`include: "failed"`) only events it did not receive — deliveries it gave up on, and events recorded while it was switched off — so repeating a call sends nothing twice. `include: "all"` also re-sends what it already received: deduplicate on `id` first. Types follow the endpoint's events now: if you added a type later, its events recorded since the endpoint was created are sent too — never sent to it before, but older than what it has received. Up to 10,000 per call; `nextSince` says where to continue. Events written at one exact moment are never split across calls, so in the rare case of more than that at one moment, a call queues them all. For code that catches up by itself, read `GET /v1/events?after=<last listed id>` instead.

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/replay`

item.name: Events
item.description: The event log: every event in this workspace, exactly as webhooks deliver it, kept 7, 30 or 90 days by plan. To catch up after downtime, ask for everything `after` the last event you read from this list (not the last webhook: webhooks arrive out of order). Needs `history:read`, on plans with webhooks.

query.description: An event id: return the events after it, oldest first. To catch up, pass the id of the last event of a list page you processed — never a webhook's id, since webhooks can arrive out of order.
Events at or after this time.
Events before this time.
Only these types: repeat it (`type=a&type=b`) or separate with commas.
Events about this MT5 account, including multi-account orders with a leg on it.
`failed`: events at least one of your endpoints has not received — given up on, or still retrying after a failure.
Without `after`: the previous page's `nextCursor`.

request.description:
Everything that happened in this workspace while its plan included webhooks, exactly as webhooks deliver it, kept 7, 30 or 90 days by plan — whether or not a webhook endpoint was listening. Events from a time the plan did not include webhooks are not recorded, so they are not listed.

An event appears in the list a few seconds after it happens, and only once every earlier event has, so a page never moves past one that has not appeared yet — except an event stuck more than 15 minutes before it could be prepared for sending (rare; we alert on it), which stops holding the list back and so, once it does appear, may fall behind an `after=` loop that already paged past its moment.

**Catching up after downtime:** keep an anchor id taken only from the last item of a list page you processed — never from a webhook: webhooks do not arrive in list order (sends run in parallel and retries are spread out), so a webhook's id can be newer than an event still retrying. On start, call `?after=<anchor>` and keep calling with the last id of each page until a page comes back empty. Then check `delivery_status=failed`, or run a replay, for anything given up on. Deduplicate on `id`. With `after`, events come oldest first. Without it, newest first, paged by `nextCursor`. An `after` id older than your plan keeps answers `400 EVENT_NOT_IN_HISTORY`: resume from `since` instead.

`GET /v1/events`

Exactly as a webhook delivery carried it.

`GET /v1/events/{id}`

item.name: Workspace
item.description: The workspace a credential belongs to: its plan, and whether trading is switched off.

item.name: The workspace this credential belongs to

request.description:
Its plan, and whether trading is switched off. Our staff switch trading off for a whole workspace only during an incident; this is where to see it.

`GET /v1/workspace`

item.name: Billing
item.description: Plans, usage, what the month would cost, invoices, and paying for a plan.

request.description:
The plans on offer now: what each includes and what it costs. Prices are in minor units — `9900` is $99.00, never a float.

`accounts` is a capacity limit: you cannot exceed it and be billed for the excess. The monthly allowances can run over where the plan allows it, up to twice the allowance, after which orders are refused — a runaway strategy should not be able to generate an unbounded invoice.

`GET /v1/plans`

item.name: This month's usage and what it would cost

request.description:
Counted as it happens rather than derived at the end of the month, so this is the same number the invoice will use.

**Over quota, opening is refused and closing is always allowed.** A billing problem must never hold you in a position you cannot exit — an order to close comes back `201` however far over the plan you are, and only opening returns `402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.

`GET /v1/billing/usage`

For a chart, or for checking an invoice line against the day it came from.

`GET /v1/billing/usage/daily`

item.name: What is paying for the plan

request.description:
The workspace's subscription, if it has one: plan, card or crypto, status, the current paid period and whether it ends at period end. Null when nothing is being paid for.

`GET /v1/billing/subscription`

Every invoice for this workspace, newest first, with its number, amount, status, provider and any refunds. Amounts are in minor units.

`GET /v1/billing/invoices`

Each with the network it must be sent on. Sending on another network loses the payment.

`GET /v1/billing/crypto/coins`

One invoice by id, with its lines, payment status and refunds. Another workspace's invoice is 404.

`GET /v1/billing/invoices/{id}`

item.name: API keys
item.description:
Issuing, renaming, re-scoping and revoking this workspace's ordinary keys. Needs an admin key (`fx_admin_…`) — or a signed-in owner or admin in the console; ordinary keys are refused. A key's secret is returned once, by the request that creates it, and never again.

This folder sends `{{adminKey}}` (an `fx_admin_…` key), not `{{apiKey}}`.

request.description:
**Needs an admin key** (`fx_admin_…`), made by the workspace owner in the console — or a signed-in owner or admin. Ordinary API keys are refused with `ADMIN_KEY_REQUIRED`.

Newest first, revoked keys included — a revocation is history worth seeing.

`GET /v1/api-keys`

**Needs an admin key** (`fx_admin_…`), made by the workspace owner in the console — or a signed-in owner or admin. Ordinary API keys are refused with `ADMIN_KEY_REQUIRED`.

Returns the key in `key`, **once**. We cannot show a key again after creation, or recover it. A lost key is replaced, not recovered.

`admin`, `keys:manage`, `members:manage` and `billing:manage` cannot be granted here, not even by an admin key. Issue narrow keys: an integration that only reads positions should hold `trading:read` and nothing else.

A console session confirms it's you first (`403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED`) only when the key can move money or accounts — `trading:execute`, `trading:reduce` or `accounts:write`. A read-only key, or one that only manages webhooks, is created without one.

`POST /v1/api-keys`

**Needs an admin key** (`fx_admin_…`), made by the workspace owner in the console — or a signed-in owner or admin. Ordinary API keys are refused with `ADMIN_KEY_REQUIRED`.

A key's name, scopes, environment label, hint and when it was last used — never the key itself, which is shown only once, when it is created.

`GET /v1/api-keys/{id}`

**Needs an admin key** (`fx_admin_…`), made by the workspace owner in the console — or a signed-in owner or admin. Ordinary API keys are refused with `ADMIN_KEY_REQUIRED`.

New scopes replace the old ones and apply from the key's next request. The key itself does not change, so nothing using it needs redeploying. A revoked key cannot be changed.

A console session confirms it's you first only when the change widens the key to a scope that can move money or accounts (`trading:execute`, `trading:reduce`, `accounts:write`) it did not already hold, or changes the limits on a key that already has some. Narrowing scopes, renaming, or adding limits to a key that had none, never asks.

`PATCH /v1/api-keys/{id}`

**Needs an admin key** (`fx_admin_…`), made by the workspace owner in the console — or a signed-in owner or admin. Ordinary API keys are refused with `ADMIN_KEY_REQUIRED`.

Refused from its very next request — there is no cache to wait for. Revoking an already-revoked key succeeds and changes nothing, so a retried revoke is safe.

`POST /v1/api-keys/{id}/revoke`

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness and readiness. No key required.

request.description:
Says the fxapis API process is up, for liveness probes and uptime monitors. Checks nothing else and never returns anything but 200; use /readyz to know whether it can serve traffic.

`GET /healthz`

Says the API can serve traffic right now, including storing and using account credentials. Returns 503 when it cannot.

`GET /readyz`
